subject: Agriculture
title: Chickens from the Jungle
description: One-minute skill: Chickens from the Jungle.

hook.text: Every chicken on earth descends from the red junglefowl of Southeast Asia. There are now 33 billion of them.

buildup.text: Junglefowl were likely first kept not for food but for cockfighting. Eggs and meat came later.

discovery.text: Chickens spread along trade routes—from Asia to Egypt to Rome. They were easy to transport and bred fast.

twist.text: Wild junglefowl lay about 12 eggs per year. Modern hens lay over 300. Breeding reshaped their biology.

climax.text: Chickens are now the world's most numerous bird—outnumbering all wild birds combined.

punchline.text: A jungle bird became the planet's most common animal.

quiz.question: How many eggs does a wild junglefowl lay per year compared to a modern hen?
